title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: customer-managed keys for direct export (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, request-based enablement, encryption prerequisites, licensing requirements and assignment command are supported. Minor corrections should distinguish the CMK section from the rest of the export documentation, clarify the documented meaning of MDEP and keep January 2027 explicitly a target.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans customer-managed key options for eDiscovery direct export, adding to existing Microsoft-managed encryption.
claims.quote: implementation of customer-managed key (CMK) options, allowing users to manage their own encryption keys for the data included in the direct export workflow in eDiscovery, adding to the Microsoft-managed encryption already in place.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; controls[1]
claims.claim: CMK direct export requires Customer Key configured through MDEP and a DEP in PolicyAssigned state.
claims.quote: Organizations that configure Customer Key through the Microsoft 365 Data-at-Rest Encryption Platform (MDEP) with a Data Encryption Policy (DEP) in policy assigned status can extend CMK protections to eDiscovery direct export packages.

claims.claim: Azure Key Vault must be configured following the standard Customer Key setup.
claims.quote: Your organization configured Azure Key Vault following the standard Customer Key setup process. For more information, see Set up Customer Key.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: When enabled, the feature encrypts exported investigation data at rest using customer-managed keys.
claims.quote: When enabled, exported investigation data is encrypted at rest using tenant-specific encryption scopes backed by customer-managed keys.

claims.claim: The encryption uses tenant-specific encryption scopes.
claims.quote: exported investigation data is encrypted at rest using tenant-specific encryption scopes backed by customer-managed keys.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Scope: Out of scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: This encryption applies only to direct exports and does not cover data at rest in an eDiscovery review set.
claims.quote: This encryption applies to direct exports only. Data at rest in an eDiscovery review set isn't included at this time.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The tenant must remain CMK enabled at the time of export.
claims.quote: Your tenant must remain CMK enabled at the time of the export.

claims.claim: Search export packages expire 14 days after export creation.
claims.quote: Search export packages expire 14 days after you create the export.

claims.claim: Expired search exports and their package data are deleted and cannot be recovered.
claims.quote: After 14 days, the export and all data contained in the export package are automatically deleted and can't be recovered.

claims.claim: The 14-day expiry is a general property of search exports, not a CMK-specific rule.
claims.quote: Search export packages expire 14 days after you create the export. ... This expiry applies only to search exports, not to review set exports.

claims.quote: Microsoft periodically validates your license count.

claims.quote: If your tenant doesn't have enough eligible licenses, encryption reverts to the default service encryption.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn publishes no licence specific to the CMK direct export option beyond the documented product prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery direct exports Customer Managed Key pricing licensing; read edisc-search-export CMK prerequisites, customer-key-set-up licensing prerequisites and the Purview service description Customer Key licensing section.

claims.claim: Learn names no charge specific to adding CMK encryption to direct exports.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery direct exports Customer Managed Key pricing licensing; read edisc-search-export, the Customer Key service description and edisc-billing. Billing documents export/data charges, not a charge for the CMK option.

claims.claim: The service description's Customer Key section does not explain the plan table's applicability to individual U.S. government clouds.
claims.quote: Searched: Customer Key, license count and Exchange or Teams in the fetched Purview service description; read Customer Key licensing and plan availability. The section lists G5/GOV plans but no GCC, GCC High or DoD-specific mapping.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The export documentation does not name U.S. government clouds for the CMK feature or specify a cloud-specific enablement route.
claims.quote: Searched: GCC, DoD, CMK and MDEP in edisc-search-export; read its CMK prerequisites and download guidance. The CMK section has no government-cloud qualification, although later download guidance names GCC and GCCH.
claims.fix: Replace 'The page does not name the US Government clouds' with 'The CMK section does not specify availability or an enablement route for GCC, GCC High or DoD.' In the checklist, refer to the CMK section rather than the whole export page.

claims.claim: No self-service administrator UI or automation operation is documented for enabling CMK direct export.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK direct exports enable admin portal PowerShell Graph; read edisc-search-export, edisc-ref-api-guide and customer-key-set-up. Found support/CSAM enablement, not a feature switch or enablement API.

claims.claim: A tenant multi-workload DEP assignment UI is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: multi-workload DEP assign admin center Customer Key; read customer-key-manage and search excerpts for Windows 365 Customer Key. The tenant DEP is assigned in PowerShell; Intune's Cloud PC encryption selector is a different control.

claims.claim: Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment -DataEncryptionPolicy <PolicyName or ID> assigns a multi-workload DEP at tenant level.
claims.quote:
After creating a multi-workload data encryption policy (DEP), assign it using the Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment cmdlet.
Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment -DataEncryptionPolicy <PolicyName or ID>
Replace <PolicyName or ID> with the name or GUID of the policy.

claims.claim: The assignment command runs through Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Exchange Online PowerShell for DEP operations

claims.claim: The Customer Key manage page requires Exchange admin permissions for DEP operations.
claims.quote: Permissions: Exchange admin permissions (all DEP operations run through Exchange Online PowerShell)

claims.claim: The assignment cmdlet is not a read-only status check.
claims.quote: Use the Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment cmdlet to assign a Microsoft 365 data-at-rest encryption policy at the tenant level.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The correctly documented multi-workload assignment control is qualified with a caveat that the export page does not explicitly name its DEP type.
claims.quote: | -Scenario | Workload: MDEP (Multiple Workloads) or EXO (Exchange) | MDEP or EXO |
claims.fix: Keep the correct command, but replace the DEP-type caveat in the note and prose with 'The export page requires a DEP assigned through MDEP; Customer Key setup identifies MDEP as Multiple Workloads.' Remove the first Open questions bullet and the checklist request to identify the DEP type. The existing cited setup page documents this mapping.

claims.claim: The CMK export documentation does not specify export behaviour when the tenant is not CMK enabled.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK direct exports PolicyAssigned tenant not enabled encryption status report; read the CMK section of edisc-search-export and Customer Key overview. Found the remain-enabled prerequisite, not the direct export failure or fallback behaviour.

claims.where: Open questions: export behaviour and encryption visibility
claims.claim: The export documentation does not identify a way to see whether a particular export was encrypted with the customer key.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK direct exports PolicyAssigned tenant not enabled encryption status report; read CMK and export details in edisc-search-export and export metadata in edisc-ref-api-guide. Found no per-export CMK verification indicator.

claims.claim: DEP assignment is a prerequisite, not the enablement setting for CMK direct export.
claims.quote: To enable this feature, contact Microsoft Support or your Customer Success Account Manager (CSAM) and request CMK for eDiscovery direct exports for your tenant. ... A Data Encryption Policy (DEP) is in PolicyAssigned state
